messages:
maya: customer reporting intermittent streaming JSON parse failures from the Go SDK when consuming /v1/responses streaming. they see: \"invalid character '\\n' looking for beginning of value\" after ~200-500 tokens. also they mentioned intermittent 401s (short-lived) and p99 latency spikes to ~3s. repro attached as logs below. asking for quick mitigation.

prateek: thanks, maya. can you paste the SDK version + go version and a tiny snippet of how they're consuming the stream? default bufio.Scanner limit often bites here. also need raw chunk bytes if possible (the exact chunk boundaries).

maya: SDK: github.com/redwood/inference-go v0.9.1, go1.19. snippet from user: 
```go
resp, _ := client.Responses.Stream(ctx, req)
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
for scanner.Scan() {
    line := scanner.Text()
    // decode JSON per-line
    var m map[string]any
    _ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &m)
}
```
they included this chunk dump (server -> client). note that one JSON object gets split across chunks: 
```
0001: {"id":"r1","delta":"Hello","meta":{
0002: "chunks":1}}
0003: {"id":"r2","delta":"World"}
```
(chunk boundaries shown). the parse error aligns with when the scanner hits the default 64k token size or sees broken framing.

prateek: yep. two things: 1) bufio.Scanner has a small default token buf (64K) and will fail on large messages or when server doesn't guarantee newline-delimited JSON; 2) using per-line Unmarshal assumes server emits full JSON objects per chunk. immediate mitigations:
- ask customer to upgrade to v0.10.2 (contains scanner.Buffer increase & fallback) OR
- change their client to use json.Decoder streaming decoder: 
```go
dec := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)
for {
    var msg map[string]any
    if err := dec.Decode(&msg); err == io.EOF { break }
    if err != nil { log.Printf("decode err: %v", err); break }
    // handle msg
}
```
this handles objects that span reads without buffer limit issues.

jordan: customer also flagged intermittent 401s — could be token refresh race. maya, did they use short-lived token rotation in their client?

maya: they do rotate tokens via our SDK's TokenSource wrapper. logs show one 401 then immediate retry succeeded. I suspect a timing window on our auth middleware or an upstream auth cache TTL. also the latency spikes correlate with times we saw partial chunk boundaries in the same request traces.

sarah: from runtime side: we recently enabled smaller write-chunk sizes to improve tail latency on heavy load; that can cause more chunk-splitting. we'll look into coalescing small writes for streaming endpoints. can you capture trace id and sample request id?

maya: trace: trace-7f3b; request id: req-9a2c. attached in the customer's upload (they shared logs).

prateek: action plan:
- support (maya): ask customer to try the json.Decoder snippet or upgrade to v0.10.2, and enable non-streaming fallback for now if they need guaranteed framing. tell them to also provide raw TCP capture if they can.
- eng-runtime (sarah): investigate chunking behavior and consider server-side coalescing or adjusting write buffer to avoid breaking JSON objects mid-object. also check if auth cache invalidation could trigger 401 window.
- infra (jordan): check token rotation path and retry timings; ensure SDK's TokenSource refresh is not racing requests.
- prateek: open issue #4023 to track Go SDK default scanner -> decoder migration and include repro from this thread.

deploy-bot: created issue redwood/go-sdk#4023 and linked trace req-9a2c.

maya: I will message the customer with the workaround + ask for pcap. will update here when they test. thanks :thumbsup:

prateek: if they can't change client quickly, we can temporarily offer them non-streaming endpoints for larger responses (supports will toggle) — ping me and I'll flip it for them.

maya: noted. marking tentatively customer-facing fix = upgrade to v0.10.2 or use decoder; long-term = runtime coalesce + SDK hardening.

sarah: I'll prioritize a short-term runtime tweak (coalesce small writes) and follow with tests to ensure it doesn't regress latency. will post update in 24h.

maya: thanks everyone. closing loop once customer confirms.
